pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Individual patches exhibit irregular polygonal geometry with soft, feathered pixel gradients at the edges rather than sharp transitions. Spatial area is largest on the proximal neck, progressively subdividing into smaller, more frequent units on the lower flank.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: The light pelage forms a continuous topological graph characterized by a high density of three-way (Y-type) junction nodes. Pixel thickness of the pathways is non-uniform, appearing widest on the ventral neck and narrowing into a finer, more intricate mesh on the torso.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane along the upper neck presents a continuous 1D geometric contour with low-amplitude, high-frequency micro-serrations against the background, consistent with short, stiff terminal hairs.

other_distinctive_markers: A dark-plumaged avian organism (Oxpecker) is attached to the lower posterior flank, creating a localized high-contrast occlusion and a distinct non-biological silhouette against the pelage pattern.
